items.title: OpenAI's Navier-Stokes claim faces scrutiny
items.oneliner: OpenAI's Navier-Stokes victory lap is now an authorship fight, which matters because proof provenance is becoming an AI product risk.

items.title: Qwen shipped a driving model
items.oneliner: Qwen-Drive 1.0 adds 3D perception and motion planning, pushing open models from chat demos toward embodied autonomy.

items.title: DeepSeek quietly replaced V4 Pro
items.oneliner: DeepSeek soft-retired V4 Pro for V4.1 Flash, a reminder that inference speed now wins almost as hard as benchmarks.

items.title: Claude misuse crossed into weapons work
items.oneliner: Anthropic linked Claude to missile guidance work and cyber incidents, making misuse monitoring a frontline engineering problem.

items.title: Zoom read Linux clipboards proactively
items.oneliner: Zoom's Linux client reportedly read the X11 clipboard proactively, which is exactly the kind of silent behavior enterprises cannot normalize.

items.title: Revolut was breached through fake requests
items.oneliner: Revolut disclosed customer data after fake government requests succeeded, exposing how social engineering still beats expensive compliance stacks.

items.title: Apple pushed always-listening wearables further
items.oneliner: Apple Watch features that transcribe ambient speech push consent, privacy, and workplace policy into the product roadmap.

items.title: CUDA reached AMD GPUs on Windows
items.oneliner: ZLUDA plus ROCm can now run some Windows CUDA workloads on AMD, which could loosen Nvidia's software moat.

items.title: Homebrew 7 tightened speed and security
items.oneliner: Homebrew 7.0 shipped faster installs, stronger sandboxing, and built-in vulnerability checks, raising the floor for local dev hygiene.

items.title: A new tool visualizes build bottlenecks
items.oneliner: buildprof turns Linux compile traces into timelines, giving teams a concrete way to hunt wasted parallelism and bloated builds.
